fixes.explanation: That's the one, friend. God says, “You are not to make any gods alongside Me; you are not to make for yourselves gods of silver or gold.” (Exodus 20:23) That comes right after He reminds them that He has spoken to them from heaven. I've stamped thousands of cookies, and not one of them ever ran my bakery.

That's the reason, and it's right there in the verse. God says, “You must not exploit or oppress a foreign resident, for you yourselves were foreigners in the land of Egypt.” (Exodus 22:21) The Israelites know what it's like to be the newcomer. God points them straight back to their own story.
Rent doesn't appear in this verse. What God says the lender must not charge is “interest.” (Exodus 22:25) The man borrowing is poor and one of God's people. So no interest goes on that loan.

Not this time, friend. God says, “…do not show favoritism to a poor man in his lawsuit.” (Exodus 23:3) A few verses later He also says, “You shall not deny justice to the poor in their lawsuits.” (Exodus 23:6) So God is telling them to keep the scales level, with no thumb pressing down on either side.

Return it, yes. God says, “…you must return it to him.” (Exodus 23:4) Even when it's your enemy's ox or donkey that has wandered off. I think walking an enemy's donkey home would feel like the longest walk of your week.

Selling a stray animal isn't the instruction. God says, “…you must return it to him.” (Exodus 23:4) That's the command even when the owner is your enemy. The ox goes home, and no sale happens on the way.

That's it. God says, “Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see and twists the words of the righteous.” (Exodus 23:8) Two things named there: it blinds people who can see, and it twists the words of the righteous. Hand a bribe to somebody with perfect eyesight and God says it still leaves them blind.

Right. God says the land rests in the seventh year “…so that the poor among your people may eat from the field and the wild animals may consume what they leave.” (Exodus 23:11) The poor eat from the field, and the wild animals get what they leave. Six years of sowing, then a whole year where the field feeds others. I can't even rest my ovens for one afternoon.

Yes, the ox and donkey are named. God says, “…on the seventh day you must cease, so that your ox and your donkey may rest and the son of your maidservant may be refreshed, as well as the foreign resident.” (Exodus 23:12) The ox, the donkey, the son of the maidservant and the foreign resident are all in that list. Even the donkey, who I'm sure has opinions.

Complaints aren't what this verse is about, friend. God says, “You must not invoke the names of other gods; they must not be heard on your lips.” (Exodus 23:13) The line is about the names of other gods. Grumbling about a long desert walk is a different kind of problem, and this verse isn't covering it.

Right. God says they eat unleavened bread for seven days in the month of Abib “…because that was the month you came out of Egypt.” (Exodus 23:15) So the reason is what happened to them in that month: they came out of Egypt. Every year the feast brings that month back around.

The law isn't given as the reason here, friend. God says they eat unleavened bread in Abib “…because that was the month you came out of Egypt.” (Exodus 23:15) The reason is the leaving, not the law. Pick that one and your bread comes out flat in all the right ways.

Yes. God says, “Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God.” (Exodus 23:19) The best of the firstfruits is what goes to His house. When guests come to my bakery, the best cookies go on the front of the tray. The broken ones are for me, and I've made peace with that.

Leftovers aren't what God asks for, friend. He says, “Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God.” (Exodus 23:19) Imagine handing someone the crumbs from the bottom of the cookie box and calling it a gift. I've been the crumbs in the bottom of a drawer, and I can tell you the best goes up front.

The smallest part isn't the instruction, friend. God says, “Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God.” (Exodus 23:19) He asks for the best of them. Nobody pulls out the tiniest cookie in the batch and says, “Here, this one's for the guest of honor.”
